text:
maria: Heads-up — saw a weird pattern this morning in us-west-2: two ~90s spot interruptions back-to-back, and our autoscaler aggressively spawned new nodes which then got reclaimed, causing a large cost blip.

sanjay: ugh. do you have the timeline/logs? was it one AZ or multi-AZ?

maria: multi-AZ but concentrated in a single instance type (p4d-like). timeline: termination notice -> immediate scale-out trigger -> new nodes requested -> more interrupts -> rinse/repeat.

ev an: can you paste the autoscaler logs? suspect our burst threshold + no cooldown is the culprit.

maria: pasted snippet from k8s events/logs:

```
2026-03-18T07:12:11Z NodeTerminationNotice: ip-10-0-3-12 (spot) 90s
2026-03-18T07:12:12Z HPA: queue_length>40 -> scale-out to 12 pods
2026-03-18T07:12:13Z ClusterAutoscaler: request 4 nodes (p4d) us-west-2a
2026-03-18T07:13:40Z NodeTerminated: ip-10-0-3-12
2026-03-18T07:13:41Z ClusterAutoscaler: detected shortages -> request 6 nodes
2026-03-18T07:14:20Z NodeCreationFailed: capacity-oversubscribe
```

maria: that loop is literally 2 minutes long. cost up 3x for those minutes.

sanjay: not great. we need interruption-smoothing to avoid replacing full capacity immediately. options: warm pool / buffer nodes, per-AZ burst caps, longer cooldowns, and prefer diversified instance families.

evan: agree. propose immediate mitigation:
- add a 300s global scale-out cooldown for spot-backed node groups
- cap max surge per AZ to 2 nodes
- keep a tiny warm-pool of 2-4 ephemeral GPUs in each AZ (cheaper instance types)
- enable NodeTerminationNotice handler to drain and prefer rebalancing rather than instant scale-out

leo: can we implement a probabilistic backoff so we don't react to single termination notices? like wait for N notices within T seconds before full-scale reaction.

sanjay: yes — "interruption smoothing": require 2 termination notices within 120s for that AZ+instance-type combo to trigger large scale-out; single notice only triggers quick pod rescheduling onto warm-pool or lower-capacity instances.

maria: also suggest we bias the scheduler to prefer heterogeneous placement (spread across instance families) for non-latency-critical batches. reduces correlated preemption.

evan: here's a draft autoscaler config patch (for k8s-cluster-autoscaler + custom policy):

```
# autoscaler-policy.yaml (excerpt)
policies:
  scaleOutCooldownSec: 300
  maxSurgePerAZ: 2
  interruptionSmoothing:
    windowSec: 120
    noticesRequired: 2
  warmPool:
    enabled: true
    sizePerAZ: 3
    instanceTypes: [g5.xlarge, g4dn.xlarge]
  diversification:
    preferHeterogeneous: true
    maxSameFamilyPercent: 40
```

maria: nice. any risk to latency SLOs if we add that cooldown?

evan: for tail-sensitive paths we can mark node pools as "latency-critical" and keep their existing aggressive policy. this change only applies to spot-backed best-effort pools.

sanjay: operational checklist:
- roll config to staging cluster and run fault injection (terminate spot instances with 30-120s offset)
- run load tests to ensure queue growth doesn't blow past HPA thresholds during cooldowns
- add dashboards: per-AZ surge events, warm-pool utilization, scale-out latency, cost delta

leo: I'll wire up dashboards + alert for surge rate > 3/min in any AZ.

autoscale-bot: deployment queued: autoscaler-policy.yaml -> staging (eta 12m) :rocket:

maria: thanks. action owner for rollout and testing?

sanjay: I'll own the rollout and the fault-injection harness. evan you do the scheduler/placement changes? leo do dashboards/alerts. maria will validate cost numbers after test.

evan: will push the placement changes and a quick canary in staging.

maria: if this looks good we should schedule a 2-week observation window before applying to prod.

sanjay: +1. also add a cheap experiment: cap per-minute node creation to 5 across all spot pools to avoid API throttles and build queueing smoothing.

leo: noted. i'll also add a synthetic test that simulates 10 term notices in 3 AZs.

maria: perfect. thanks team. :thumbsup:

autoscale-bot: deployment started -> staging cluster (1792345690)

maria: leaving notes in the runbook under "interruption-smoothing".
